events.text:
```python
template = "hikes/_form.html" if request.headers.get("HX-Request") else "hikes/create.html"
return render(request, template, {"form": form})
```

When htmx posts, it sends an `HX-Request` header, so the view now returns only `_form.html` on validation errors and your `hx-target="this" hx-swap="outerHTML"` replaces just the form. On success it answers 204 with `HX-Redirect` so htmx does a normal navigation to the detail page. Make sure `_form.html` contains the `<form>` tag itself, otherwise you'll get a form nested inside a form after the swap. If you end up doing this in many views, `django-htmx` gives you `request.htmx` instead of reading the header by hand.

hikes = (

`select_related` for trail and region: they're foreign keys, so Django joins them into the same query instead of 2 extra queries per row (that's ~4k queries today for 2k hikes). `prefetch_related` is for the many-to-many tags, which can't be joined; it does one extra query for all of them. # Payments architecture

Last updated: 2026-08-28 (Marco)

## Overview

Agencies get paid by their clients through Acme invoices. We never handle
raw card numbers.

## Checkout

Checkout uses Stripe Checkout in redirect mode. The web app creates a
Checkout Session through the API and redirects the browser to Stripe. The
web app never sees card data; it only receives the session id on the
success URL.

## Webhooks

Stripe calls POST /v1/webhooks/stripe. The API verifies the signature,
stores the event in stripe_events (idempotent on event id), and enqueues
a job to update the invoice status.

## Payouts

When Stripe pays out to an agency's connected account, the payout.paid
webhook creates a row in payouts. Agencies see their payouts in the
dashboard under Settings > Payouts.

## Open questions

- Do we backfill payouts created before the connected-account migration?

# apps/web

The Acme customer dashboard.

## Stack

- Auth: Clerk (we moved off Auth0 in August; see ACME-171). Middleware is in
  middleware.ts.
- Hosting: the web app deploys on Vercel. Every PR gets a preview deployment;

events.text: random q, whats the actual difference between useTransition and useDeferredValue? i always mix them up

```tsx
const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();
startTransition(() => setFilter(next));      // you control the update

const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(query); // you only have the value
```

`useTransition` wraps a state update you trigger and marks it low priority, and gives you `isPending`. `useDeferredValue` is for when you receive a value (often a prop) and want a lagging copy of it, so the expensive part re-renders later while the input stays snappy. Same mechanism underneath; pick by whether you own the setter.
